title: Near-Optimal Generalized Sorting in Haskell: A Comparison-Based Introsort with In-Place Merge Fallback
author: Mateus Yonathan

abstract: We present a Haskell implementation of a near-optimal generalized sorting algorithm that combines introspective quicksort, median-of-three pivot selection, and an in-place merge-sort fallback. The algorithm preserves total order, guarantees permutation invariance, and achieves an average-case complexity of $O(N\log N)$ while limiting the worst-case to $O(N\log N)$ through a depth-controlled recursion. Formal invariants are proved for total order preservation and permutation invariance, and the implementation is verified by static abstract syntax tree (AST) inspection and structural complexity profiling. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/haskell-functional-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261107_070229_a_near-optimal_generalized_sor}.
